Sources:

[abudawud:4782] Sunan Abi Dawud 4782
Grading: Sahih (Al-Albani); Sahih (Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid); Sahih (Zubair Ali Zai)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ حَنْبَلٍ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مُعَاوِيَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا دَاوُدُ بْنُ أَبِي هِنْدٍ، عَنْ أَبِي حَرْبِ بْنِ الأَسْوَدِ، عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ، قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ لَنَا ‏ "‏ إِذَا غَضِبَ أَحَدُكُمْ وَهُوَ قَائِمٌ فَلْيَجْلِسْ فَإِنْ ذَهَبَ عَنْهُ الْغَضَبُ وَإِلاَّ فَلْيَضْطَجِعْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏

[tirmidhi:1971] Jami at-Tirmidhi 1971
Grading: Sahih (Ahmad Muhammad Shakir); Sahih (Al-Albani); Hasan Sahih (Bashar Awad Maarouf)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا هَنَّادٌ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مُعَاوِيَةَ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ شَقِيقِ بْنِ سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالصِّدْقِ فَإِنَّ الصِّدْقَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْبِرِّ وَإِنَّ الْبِرَّ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ وَمَا يَزَالُ الرَّجُلُ يَصْدُقُ وَيَتَحَرَّى الصِّدْقَ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ صِدِّيقًا وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَالْكَذِبَ فَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْفُجُورِ وَإِنَّ الْفُجُورَ يَهْدِي إِلَى النَّارِ وَمَا يَزَالُ الْعَبْدُ يَكْذِبُ وَيَتَحَرَّى الْكَذِبَ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ كَذَّابًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَفِي الْبَابِ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقِ وَعُمَرَ وَعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الشِّخِّيرِ وَابْنِ عُمَرَ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو عِيسَى هَذَا حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ صَحِيحٌ ‏.‏

[malik:1826] Muwatta Malik 1826
Grading: Mauquf Daif (Salim al-Hilali)
(ar) وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، كَانَ يَقُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالصِّدْقِ فَإِنَّ الصِّدْقَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْبِرِّ وَالْبِرَّ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَالْكَذِبَ فَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْفُجُورِ وَالْفُجُورَ يَهْدِي إِلَى النَّارِ أَلاَ تَرَى أَنَّهُ يُقَالُ صَدَقَ وَبَرَّ وَكَذَبَ وَفَجَرَ ‏.‏

[muslim:6637] Sahih Muslim 6637 (Abd al-Baqi no. 2607a)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا زُهَيْرُ بْنُ حَرْبٍ، وَعُثْمَانُ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، وَإِسْحَاقُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ إِسْحَاقُ أَخْبَرَنَا وَقَالَ الآخَرَانِ، حَدَّثَنَا جَرِيرٌ، عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ، عَنْ أَبِي وَائِلٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ إِنَّ الصِّدْقَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْبِرِّ وَإِنَّ الْبِرَّ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ وَإِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيَصْدُقُ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ صِدِّيقًا وَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْفُجُورِ وَإِنَّ الْفُجُورَ يَهْدِي إِلَى النَّارِ وَإِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيَكْذِبُ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ كَذَّابًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏

Question: how does being honest actually lead someone to jannah? is there a hadith on this

The Prophet ﷺ described a chain: truthfulness guides to righteousness, and righteousness guides to Paradise, and a man keeps speaking the truth and striving for it until he is written with Allah as a truthful person [tirmidhi:1971]. The opposite chain is also given: lying guides to wickedness, wickedness guides to the Fire, and a person who keeps lying is written down as a liar [tirmidhi:1971]. The same teaching is narrated in Sahih Muslim, where truth leads to righteousness and then to Paradise, and lying leads to wickedness and then to the Fire [muslim:6637]. So honesty is not a single act but a habit that shapes a person until it becomes their record with Allah [tirmidhi:1971].

[abudawud:3257] Sunan Abi Dawud 3257
Grading: Sahih (Al-Albani); Sahih (Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid); Sahih (Shuaib Al Arnaut)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو تَوْبَةَ الرَّبِيعُ بْنُ نَافِعٍ، حَدَّثَنَا مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ سَلاَّمٍ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي أَبُو قِلاَبَةَ، أَنَّ ثَابِتَ بْنَ الضَّحَّاكِ، أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّهُ، بَايَعَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ مَنْ حَلَفَ بِمِلَّةٍ غَيْرِ مِلَّةِ الإِسْلاَمِ كَاذِبًا فَهُوَ كَمَا قَالَ وَمَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسَهُ بِشَىْءٍ عُذِّبَ بِهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَلَيْسَ عَلَى رَجُلٍ نَذْرٌ فِيمَا لاَ يَمْلِكُهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏

Question: What should I do if I get angry while I'm standing?

The Prophet ﷺ said that if one of you becomes angry while standing, he should sit down; if the anger goes, that is enough, and if not, he should lie down [abudawud:4782]. The advice is to change your posture to calm yourself, moving from standing to sitting and then to lying down if needed [abudawud:4782].

Question: Who is the strong person according to the Prophet? not talking about gym strength lol

The Prophet ﷺ said the strong one is not the one who throws others in wrestling, but the one who controls himself when angry: "إِنَّمَا الشَّدِيدُ الَّذِي يَمْلِكُ نَفْسَهُ عِنْدَ الْغَضَبِ" [muslim:6643]. In another narration he asked his companions whom they counted as a wrestler, and when they said the man whom men cannot throw, he said no, it is the one who masters himself when angry [abudawud:4779]. So real strength in these narrations is self-control at the moment of anger, not physical power [muslim:6643].

Question: Is gentleness really rewarded more than being harsh? I tend to be blunt with people

Yes. The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah is Gentle, loves gentleness, and gives for gentleness what He does not give for harshness [ibnmajah:3688]. A similar wording is narrated in Sunan Abi Dawud: Allah is gentle, loves gentleness and grants for it what He does not grant for harshness [abudawud:4807]. He ﷺ also warned that whoever is deprived of gentleness is deprived of good [ibnmajah:3687]. Being blunt is therefore something to work on, since gentleness carries a reward that harshness does not [abudawud:4807].

Question: What is the punishment for spreading tales between people (namimah)?

The Prophet ﷺ said plainly that a tale-carrier will not enter Paradise: "لاَ يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ نَمَّامٌ" [muslim:290]. In another narration he passed by two graves and said both men were being punished, though not for something they thought major; one did not guard himself from his urine and the other used to go about spreading tales [tirmidhi:70]. He ﷺ also described tale-carrying as the kind of talk that spreads among people to stir trouble between them [muslim:6636]. These narrations show it is a serious sin with consequences in the grave and the Hereafter [tirmidhi:70].

Question: how much does islam emphasize treating neighbours well? my neighbour is kind of annoying

The emphasis is very strong. The Prophet ﷺ said that Jibril kept advising him about the neighbour until he thought he would make the neighbour an heir [ibnmajah:3674]. Aishah narrated the same meaning in Sahih Muslim [muslim:6685]. He ﷺ also gave a practical instruction to Abu Dharr: when you cook broth, add more water to it and look after your neighbours [muslim:6688]. These narrations do not make good treatment depend on the neighbour being pleasant; the instruction is general [ibnmajah:3674].

Question: How many days am I obliged to host a guest, and after that can I ask them to pay for food?

The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honour his guest, that the guest's special due is a day and a night, that hospitality is three days, and that what comes after that is charity [abudawud:3748]. He ﷺ also said it is not lawful for the guest to stay so long that he puts his host in difficulty [abudawud:3748]. I'm not sure about charging a guest for food after the three days; these sources only describe anything beyond three days as charity and do not discuss asking for payment.

Question: is smiling at someone really counted as charity?

Yes. The Prophet ﷺ said every good deed is charity, and among good deeds is meeting your brother with a cheerful face and pouring water from your bucket into his vessel [tirmidhi:1970]. So a cheerful face toward a fellow Muslim is itself a good deed that is counted as sadaqah, even without spending money [tirmidhi:1970].

Question: Hadith about Allah showing mercy to people who are merciful?

The Prophet ﷺ said the Most Merciful shows mercy to those who are merciful, and that if you show mercy to those on earth, the One above the heaven will show mercy to you [abudawud:4941]. Tirmidhi records the same hadith with an addition: the womb (ties of kinship) takes its name from Ar-Rahman, so whoever keeps it joined, Allah keeps him joined, and whoever cuts it, Allah cuts him off [tirmidhi:1924]. Mercy toward others is therefore tied directly to receiving Allah's mercy [tirmidhi:1924].

Question: Can a person curse his own parents without directly doing it? Heard something like that

Yes, the Prophet ﷺ described exactly this. He said that cursing one's parents is among the greatest sins, and when the companions asked how a man could curse his parents, he explained that a man insults another man's father, so that man insults his father, and he insults his mother, so the other insults his mother [tirmidhi:1902]. Sahih Muslim records the same explanation, calling the abuse of one's parents a major sin [muslim:263]. So insulting other people's parents counts as bringing insult on your own [muslim:263].

Question: What are the three signs of a munafiq?

The Prophet ﷺ said the signs of a hypocrite are that when he speaks he lies, when he makes a promise he breaks it, and when he is trusted he betrays [tirmidhi:2631]. These three are lying in speech, breaking promises, and betraying a trust, and the hadith presents them as marks of hypocrisy to be avoided [tirmidhi:2631].

Question: story of the ansari man who turned off the lamp for his guest?

A man from the Ansar had a guest stay the night, but he only had enough food for himself and his children [tirmidhi:3304]. He told his wife to put the children to sleep, put out the lamp, and serve the guest what they had [tirmidhi:3304]. The verse "ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة" was then revealed about them, praising those who prefer others over themselves even when in need [tirmidhi:3304]. Sahih Muslim narrates the same incident of the Ansari who had only enough for himself and his children [muslim:5360].

(ar) حَدَّثَنَا هَنَّادٌ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مُعَاوِيَةَ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ شَقِيقِ بْنِ سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالصِّدْقِ فَإِنَّ الصِّدْقَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْبِرِّ وَإِنَّ الْبِرَّ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ وَمَا يَزَالُ الرَّجُلُ يَصْدُقُ وَيَتَحَرَّى الصِّدْقَ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ صِدِّيقًا وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَالْكَذِبَ فَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْفُجُورِ وَإِنَّ الْفُجُورَ يَهْدِي إِلَى النَّارِ وَمَا يَزَالُ الْعَبْدُ يَكْذِبُ وَيَتَحَرَّى الْكَذِبَ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ كَذَّابًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَفِي الْبَابِ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقِ وَعُمَرَ وَعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الشِّخِّيرِ وَابْنِ عُمَرَ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو عِيسَى هَذَا حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ صَحِيحٌ ‏.‏

[tirmidhi:2631] Jami at-Tirmidhi 2631
Grading: Sahih (Al-Albani); Sahih - Bukhari And Muslim (Zubair Ali Zai)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو حَفْصٍ، عَمْرُو بْنُ عَلِيٍّ حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ، عَنِ الْعَلاَءِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ آيَةُ الْمُنَافِقِ ثَلاَثٌ إِذَا حَدَّثَ كَذَبَ وَإِذَا وَعَدَ أَخْلَفَ وَإِذَا اؤْتُمِنَ خَانَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو عِيسَى هَذَا حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ غَرِيبٌ مِنْ حَدِيثِ الْعَلاَءِ وَقَدْ رُوِيَ مِنْ غَيْرِ وَجْهٍ عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏ وَفِي الْبَابِ عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ وَأَنَسٍ وَجَابِرٍ ‏.‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ حُجْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي سُهَيْلِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَحْوَهُ بِمَعْنَاهُ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو عِيسَى هَذَا حَدِيثٌ صَحِيحٌ وَأَبُو سُهَيْلٍ هُوَ عَمُّ مَالِكِ بْنِ أَنَسٍ وَاسْمُهُ نَافِعُ بْنُ مَالِكِ بْنِ أَبِي عَامِرٍ الأَصْبَحِيُّ الْخَوْلاَنِيُّ ‏.‏

[رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ] Question: What does Islam say about anger, and is there a specific dua to say when angry?

A man asked the Prophet ﷺ for advice, and he told him repeatedly not to become angry [nawawi:16]. He ﷺ also said the truly strong one is the one who controls himself when angry [abudawud:4779], and advised that someone angry while standing should sit, and if it does not leave, lie down [abudawud:4782]. I'm not sure about a specific dua to say when angry, since none of these sources mentions one.

Question: Is it a sin if I have money but keep delaying paying back what I owe?

Yes. The Prophet ﷺ said that delay in paying a debt by someone who is able to pay is injustice ("مَطْلُ الْغَنِيِّ ظُلْمٌ") [muslim:4002]. So a person with the means should not postpone repayment, because the hadith calls that delay a wrong done to the lender [muslim:4002].

Question: What happens to someone who dies while still in debt?

The Prophet ﷺ said the believer's soul is held suspended by his debt until it is paid off for him [tirmidhi:1078]. He also said that whoever dies free of three things, arrogance, stealing from war booty, and debt, will enter Paradise [ibnmajah:2412]. The seriousness is shown in practice: when a man in debt was brought for funeral prayer, the Prophet ﷺ told the people to pray for their companion, and he only prayed himself after Abu Qatadah promised to pay the debt in full [nasai:1960]. This is why the heirs or others are encouraged to settle a dead person's debts quickly [tirmidhi:1078].

Question: my shop has some damaged stock, can i just mix it in with the good stuff and sell it?

No, hiding a defect is cheating. The Prophet ﷺ passed a pile of food, put his hand inside and found it wet; the seller said rain had fallen on it, and he ﷺ asked why he had not put the wet part on top so people could see it, then said whoever cheats is not one of us [tirmidhi:1315]. Ibn Majah records a similar incident where he found something wrong in food being sold and said that the one who cheats is not one of us [ibnmajah:2224]. So the damaged goods should be shown openly to the buyer, not mixed in to hide them [tirmidhi:1315].

Question: Does the hadith against hoarding apply to every product, or only to food?

The Prophet ﷺ said that no one withholds goods to raise their price except a sinner [abudawud:3447]. In the same report, Ahmad was asked what hoarding is and said it is what people live on, and al-Awza'i described the hoarder as one who withholds supply from the market [abudawud:3447]. Tirmidhi notes that the people of knowledge disliked hoarding food, while some of them allowed it in things other than food, and Ibn al-Mubarak saw no harm in storing cotton and hides [tirmidhi:1267]. He also reports that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, a narrator of the hadith, would store oil and fodder [tirmidhi:1267]. So the scope was understood differently; a qualified scholar should be asked about a specific product.

Question: swearing by allah to convince customers to buy, is that a problem?

Yes, it is warned against. The Prophet ﷺ said that swearing may get a product sold but it wipes out the blessing [muslim:4125]. Abu Qatadah heard him say: beware of swearing a lot when selling, for it promotes the sale and then destroys the blessing [nasai:4460]. Ibn Majah has the same warning against swearing oaths in trade [ibnmajah:2209]. So even if an oath brings a quick sale, these narrations say the earnings lose their barakah [nasai:4460].

Question: Will an honest businessman be with the prophets on judgement day? Also, is investing in shares halal?

There is a narration in Ibn Majah that the trustworthy, honest Muslim merchant will be with the martyrs on the Day of Resurrection, but its grade is weak (Da'if) [ibnmajah:2139]. A sahih narration says Allah has mercy on a person who is lenient when he sells, when he buys and when he asks for repayment [ibnmajah:2203]. I'm not sure about investing in shares; none of these sources discusses it, so please ask a qualified scholar.

Question: Once I agree on a deal can I still back out?

According to the hadith, the buyer and seller each keep the option to cancel as long as they have not separated, or unless they agreed on an option [tirmidhi:1245]. Nafi' added that Ibn Umar, when he bought something while seated, would stand up and leave so that the sale became binding [tirmidhi:1245].

(en) And when We said unto the angels: Prostrate yourselves before Adam, they fell prostrate, all save Iblis. He demurred through pride, and so became a disbeliever

Question: Why did Iblis refuse to bow to Adam?

Allah says the angels fell prostrate before Adam, "all save Iblis, who was not of those who make prostration" [quran:7:11]. When Allah asked what stopped him, Iblis said: "I am better than him. Thou createdst me of fire while him Thou didst create of mud" [quran:7:12]. Another verse says he refused out of pride and so became a disbeliever: "He demurred through pride, and so became a disbeliever" [quran:2:34]. So his refusal came from arrogance based on what he was created from [quran:7:12].

Question: What words did Adam say when he repented?

Allah says that Adam received words from his Lord and He relented toward him [quran:2:37]. Jalalayn explains that these words were "ربنا ظلمنا أنفسنا", the verse of Surat al-A'raf, and that Adam prayed with them and his repentance was accepted [jalalayn:2:37]. That verse reads: "Our Lord! We have wronged ourselves. If thou forgive us not and have not mercy on us, surely we are of the lost" [quran:7:23]. It is a supplication any believer can use when seeking forgiveness [quran:7:23].

(ar) حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ حَبِيبِ بْنِ عَرَبِيٍّ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا الْمُعْتَمِرُ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ أَبِي صَالِحٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ احْتَجَّ آدَمُ وَمُوسَى فَقَالَ مُوسَى يَا آدَمُ أَنْتَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ اللَّهُ بِيَدِهِ وَنَفَخَ فِيكَ مِنْ رُوحِهِ أَغْوَيْتَ النَّاسَ وَأَخْرَجْتَهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقَالَ آدَمُ وَأَنْتَ مُوسَى الَّذِي اصْطَفَاكَ اللَّهُ بِكَلاَمِهِ أَتَلُومُنِي عَلَى عَمَلٍ عَمِلْتُهُ كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَىَّ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضَ قَالَ فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو عِيسَى وَفِي الْبَابِ عَنْ عُمَرَ وَجُنْدَبٍ ‏.‏ وَهَذَا حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ صَحِيحٌ غَرِيبٌ مِنْ هَذَا الْوَجْهِ مِنْ حَدِيثِ سُلَيْمَانَ التَّيْمِيِّ عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ ‏.‏ وَقَدْ رَوَى بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِ الأَعْمَشِ عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ عَنْ أَبِي صَالِحٍ عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَحْوَهُ ‏.‏ وَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ عَنْ أَبِي صَالِحٍ عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏ وَقَدْ رُوِيَ هَذَا الْحَدِيثُ مِنْ غَيْرِ وَجْهٍ عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏

Question: story of adam and musa arguing about leaving paradise?

The Prophet ﷺ said that Adam and Musa argued: Musa said that Allah had created Adam with His Hand and breathed into him of His spirit, yet he caused people to be expelled from Paradise [tirmidhi:2134]. Adam replied that Musa was the one Allah chose for His speech, and asked whether he blamed him for something Allah had decreed for him before creating the heavens and the earth [tirmidhi:2134]. The Prophet ﷺ said that Adam won the argument [tirmidhi:2134]. Ibn Majah narrates the same debate between them [ibnmajah:80].

Question: How tall was Adam when he was created?

The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah created Adam sixty cubits tall [bukhari:3326]. He added that everyone who enters Paradise will be in the form of Adam, and that people have kept decreasing in stature since then [bukhari:3326]. In the same hadith, Allah told Adam to greet a group of angels, and their reply became the greeting of his descendants [bukhari:3326].

Question: where does the islamic greeting assalamu alaikum come from?

It goes back to Adam. The Prophet ﷺ said that when Allah created Adam, He told him to go and greet a group of angels and listen to their reply, because it would be his greeting and the greeting of his descendants [bukhari:3326]. Adam said "السلام عليكم" and they answered "السلام عليك ورحمة الله", adding "ورحمة الله" to it [bukhari:3326]. Sahih Muslim records the same account of Adam being told to greet the group of angels [muslim:7163].

Question: How long did Nuh call his people, and what happened to his son?

Allah says Nuh stayed among his people "a thousand years save fifty years" before the flood seized them [quran:29:14]. During the flood he called to his son, who was standing apart, to ride with them and not be with the disbelievers [quran:11:42]. The son said he would take refuge on a mountain, Nuh told him nothing protects from Allah's command that day except His mercy, and the wave came between them and he was among the drowned [quran:11:43]. When Nuh then asked about him, Jalalayn explains that Allah told him the son was not of his family that would be saved, because he was a disbeliever [jalalayn:11:46].

Question: Ibrahim was thrown in the fire right? did the fire not burn him at all?

Yes, his people said: "Burn him and stand by your gods" [quran:21:68]. Allah then said: "O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham" [quran:21:69]. Jalalayn explains that the fire burned nothing of him except the ropes that bound him; its heat left while its light remained, and because Allah also said "peace", he was kept safe from dying of its coldness [jalalayn:21:69].

Question: Which son was Ibrahim told to sacrifice, Ismail or Ishaq?

The Quran tells of Ibrahim seeing in a dream that he must sacrifice his son, and the son replying "O my father! Do that which thou art commanded" [quran:37:102]. Allah then says: "Then We ransomed him with a tremendous victim" [quran:37:107]. The verses do not name the son. Jalalayn says the one commanded to be sacrificed was Ismail or Ishaq, and that there are two opinions on this [jalalayn:37:107]. He adds that the ransom was a ram from Paradise brought by Jibril [jalalayn:37:107]. Since the sources mention both views without settling it, please ask a qualified scholar if you want to study the evidence further.

Question: When ibrahim looked at the star and said this is my lord, did he actually believe that?

Allah says that when night came Ibrahim saw a star and said "This is my Lord", but when it set he said "I love not things that set" [quran:6:76]. Jalalayn explains that he was speaking to his people, who were star-worshippers, meaning that it was their lord by their own claim, and that a lord cannot change or move because those are features of created things [jalalayn:6:76]. After the moon and the sun also set, he declared: "O my people! Lo! I am free from all that ye associate (with Him)" [quran:6:78].

Question: Did Musa murder someone before he became a prophet?

Allah says Musa entered the city and found two men fighting, one from his people and one from his enemies, and when the first asked for help, Musa struck the other and he died [quran:28:15]. Jalalayn explains that he struck him with his fist, that he was very strong, and that he did not intend to kill him [jalalayn:28:15]. Musa then said: "My Lord! Lo! I have wronged my soul, so forgive me. Then He forgave him" [quran:28:16]. So the sources describe it as an unintended killing for which he sought and received forgiveness [quran:28:16].

Question: Why did khidr kill the boy in the story with musa?

The Prophet ﷺ said that the boy whom al-Khidr killed was created a disbeliever on the day he was created [tirmidhi:3150]. Ubayy ibn Ka'b explained that had the boy lived, he would have pushed his parents into transgression and disbelief [abudawud:4705]. Abu Dawud also narrates that al-Khidr saw the boy playing with other children and killed him, and Musa objected that he had killed an innocent soul [abudawud:4707]. So the act was based on knowledge Allah gave al-Khidr about the boy's future [tirmidhi:3150].

Question: What miracles did Isa perform according to the Quran?

Allah says Isa told the Children of Israel: "I fashion for you out of clay the likeness of a bird, and I breathe into it and it is a bird, by Allah's leave" [quran:3:49]. Jalalayn explains that he did this as a sign proving his truthfulness, and that it happened by Allah's will [jalalayn:3:49]. As a baby he also spoke, saying: "Lo! I am the slave of Allah. He hath given me the Scripture and hath appointed me a Prophet" [quran:19:30].

Question: Will Isa come back before the day of judgement? what will he do

Yes. The Prophet ﷺ swore that the son of Mary will soon descend among the Muslims as a just judge [muslim:389]. He will break the cross, kill the pigs and abolish the jizyah, and wealth will become so plentiful that no one will accept it [muslim:389]. Another narration in Sahih Muslim confirms with an oath that he will certainly descend as a just judge [muslim:391]. Question: Is it wrong to say our Prophet is better than Yunus?

The Prophet ﷺ said that no one should say that he is better than Yunus ibn Matta [bukhari:3416]. Question: how much hotter is jahannam's fire compared to fire in this world?

The Prophet ﷺ said that the fire which the children of Adam kindle is one part out of seventy parts of the heat of Hell [tirmidhi:2589]. The companions said that this world's fire would already have been enough, and he replied that Hell's fire exceeds it by sixty-nine parts, each of them like its heat [tirmidhi:2589]. Abu Sa'id narrated the same meaning: your fire is one of seventy parts of the fire of Hell, each part as hot as it [tirmidhi:2590].

Question: Who will have the lightest punishment in hell?

The Prophet ﷺ said the person in the Fire punished least is a man with two burning coals placed under his feet that make his brain boil [tirmidhi:2604]. Even this lightest punishment is described as severe, which shows how serious the Fire is [tirmidhi:2604].

Question: What will the lowest person in jannah get? I heard its huge

The Prophet ﷺ said Musa asked his Lord about the lowest in rank among the people of Paradise, and Allah said it is the man who enters last, after people have taken their places [muslim:466]. He will be asked whether he would be pleased to have the like of the kingdom of one of the kings of this world, and when he says he is pleased, Allah will give him that and more like it [muslim:466]. Ibn Mas'ud also narrated that the Prophet ﷺ knew the last person to come out of the Fire and the last to enter Paradise [ibnmajah:4339].

Question: is it true death itself will be slaughtered on judgement day?

Yes. The Prophet ﷺ said death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and made to stand on the Sirat, then the people of Paradise and the people of Hell will be called and will recognise it as death [ibnmajah:4327]. It will then be slaughtered on the Sirat, and both groups will be told that their state is eternal and there will be no more death [ibnmajah:4327]. Aishah also asked where people will be on the day the earth is changed, and he ﷺ said they will be on the Sirat [ibnmajah:4279].

Question: what is the first thing we will be questioned about on the day of judgement?

The Prophet ﷺ said the first thing a servant will be held to account for is the prayer, and the first matter judged between people is bloodshed [nasai:3991]. He also said that if a person's obligatory prayer is found lacking, Allah will say to look for any voluntary prayers he did, so that they can complete it [nasai:467]. Tirmidhi records that the first cases judged between people will be those of bloodshed [tirmidhi:1396]. So the prayer comes first in a person's own account, and bloodshed comes first among disputes between people [nasai:3991].

Question: if everything is already written by Allah then why should I even bother doing good deeds?

This exact question was put to the Prophet ﷺ. Suraqah ibn Malik asked whether deeds happen by what the pens have already written and the decree has run, or by something new, and he ﷺ said it is by what the pens have written [muslim:6735]. When Suraqah asked then why act, he replied: "اعْمَلُوا فَكُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ", act, for each person is eased toward what he was created for [muslim:6735]. Ibn Majah records the same answer, that everyone is facilitated for what he was created for [ibnmajah:91]. So the decree does not cancel effort; the sources tell us to act [ibnmajah:91].

Question: what does the angel write for a baby in the womb?

The Prophet ﷺ said that after the drop has been in the womb forty or forty-five nights, the angel asks his Lord whether the person will be wretched or happy, and it is written [muslim:6725]. He asks whether it will be male or female, and that is written, along with his deeds, his lifespan and his provision, then the scroll is rolled up with nothing added or taken away [muslim:6725]. Bukhari also narrates that Allah appoints an angel over every womb who addresses his Lord at each stage of its growth [bukhari:318].

[tirmidhi:2139] Jami at-Tirmidhi 2139
Grading: Hasan (Ahmad Muhammad Shakir); Hasan (Al-Albani); Hasan (Bashar Awad Maarouf)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ الرَّازِيُّ، وَسَعِيدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ، قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ، عَنْ أَبِي مَوْدُودٍ، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ التَّيْمِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي عُثْمَانَ النَّهْدِيِّ، عَنْ سَلْمَانَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ لاَ يَرُدُّ الْقَضَاءَ إِلاَّ الدُّعَاءُ وَلاَ يَزِيدُ فِي الْعُمُرِ إِلاَّ الْبِرُّ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو عِيسَى وَفِي الْبَابِ عَنْ أَبِي أُسَيْدٍ ‏.‏ وَهَذَا حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ غَرِيبٌ مِنْ حَدِيثِ سَلْمَانَ لاَ نَعْرِفُهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ حَدِيثِ يَحْيَى بْنِ الضُّرَيْسِ ‏.‏ وَأَبُو مَوْدُودٍ اثْنَانِ أَحَدُهُمَا يُقَالُ لَهُ فِضَّةٌ وَهُوَ الَّذِي رَوَى هَذَا الْحَدِيثَ اسْمُهُ فِضَّةٌ بَصْرِيٌّ وَالآخَرُ عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ بْنُ أَبِي سُلَيْمَانَ أَحَدُهُمَا بَصْرِيٌّ وَالآخَرُ مَدَنِيٌّ وَكَانَا فِي عَصْرٍ وَاحِدٍ وابو مودود الذي روى هذا الحديث أسمه فضة بصري. ‏

Grading: Hasan (Al-Albani); Hasan (Muhammad Fouad Abd al-Baqi); Hasan Lighairihi (Shuaib Al Arnaut)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا وَكِيعٌ، عَنْ سُفْيَانَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي الْجَعْدِ، عَنْ ثَوْبَانَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ ‏ "‏ لاَ يَزِيدُ فِي الْعُمْرِ إِلاَّ الْبِرُّ وَلاَ يَرُدُّ الْقَدَرَ إِلاَّ الدُّعَاءُ وَإِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيُحْرَمُ الرِّزْقَ بِالذَّنْبِ يُصِيبُهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏

[muslim:6725] Sahih Muslim 6725 (Abd al-Baqi no. 2644)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ نُمَيْرٍ، وَزُهَيْرُ بْنُ حَرْبٍ، - وَاللَّفْظُ لاِبْنِ نُمَيْرٍ - قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ بْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ دِينَارٍ، عَنْ أَبِي الطُّفَيْلِ، عَنْ حُذَيْفَةَ بْنِ أَسِيدٍ، يَبْلُغُ بِهِ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ يَدْخُلُ الْمَلَكُ عَلَى النُّطْفَةِ بَعْدَ مَا تَسْتَقِرُّ فِي الرَّحِمِ بِأَرْبَعِينَ أَوْ خَمْسَةٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً فَيَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ أَشَقِيٌّ أَوْ سَعِيدٌ فَيُكْتَبَانِ فَيَقُولُ أَىْ رَبِّ أَذَكَرٌ أَوْ أُنْثَى فَيُكْتَبَانِ وَيُكْتَبُ عَمَلُهُ وَأَثَرُهُ وَأَجَلُهُ وَرِزْقُهُ ثُمَّ تُطْوَى الصُّحُفُ فَلاَ يُزَادُ فِيهَا وَلاَ يُنْقَصُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏

Question: Can dua change my qadar? Like if I make dua to marry a specific person will it happen?

The Prophet ﷺ said that nothing turns back the decree except supplication, and nothing increases the lifespan except righteousness; this hadith is graded Hasan [tirmidhi:2139]. Ibn Majah has a similar Hasan narration that nothing averts the divine decree except dua [ibnmajah:4022]. I'm not sure whether a dua to marry a particular person will be answered as asked; these sources do not speak about that, so please ask a qualified scholar about it.

Question: How many cups are there at the Prophet's hawd?

The Prophet ﷺ said that at his Hawd there are drinking vessels as numerous as the stars of the sky [tirmidhi:2442]. The hadith gives a comparison with the stars rather than an exact count [tirmidhi:2442]. The narration uses the stars of the sky to convey how plentiful those vessels are [tirmidhi:2442].

Question: Do the kids of non-Muslims who die young go to jannah or not?

When the Prophet ﷺ was asked about the children of the polytheists, he said that Allah knows best what they would have done [muslim:6763]. The same answer is narrated in Sunan an-Nasa'i [nasai:1949]. He also said that every child is born upon the fitrah, and it is the parents who make him a Jew or a Christian [muslim:6762]. I'm not sure about a final ruling on whether they enter Paradise; these sources leave the matter to Allah's knowledge and do not state it.

Question: Did Prophet Muhammad see Allah during the Miraj?

The sources show different positions. Aishah said that whoever tells you Muhammad saw his Lord has lied, and she recited "لاَ تُدْرِكُهُ الأَبْصَارُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ الأَبْصَارَ" as her evidence [bukhari:4855]. Abu Dharr asked the Prophet ﷺ whether he saw his Lord and he answered: "نُورٌ أَنَّى أَرَاهُ" [muslim:443]. On the other side, Ikrimah reports Ibn Abbas saying that Muhammad saw his Lord twice, but this chain is graded weak (Da'if) [tirmidhi:3279]. Jalalayn, for its part, explains the verse of Surat an-Najm about what the heart saw as referring to the Prophet seeing Jibril in his true form [jalalayn:53:11]. Since companions differed, please consult a qualified scholar for a fuller discussion.

Question: Who was the first person to accept Islam, Abu Bakr or Ali?

The narrations differ. Zaid ibn Arqam said the first to accept Islam was Ali, but when this was mentioned to Ibrahim an-Nakha'i he rejected it and said the first was Abu Bakr as-Siddiq [tirmidhi:3735]. Ibn Abbas is reported saying the first to pray was Ali, though graders differ on this chain, some calling it weak [tirmidhi:3734]. Tirmidhi notes that the people of knowledge differed: some said Abu Bakr, some said Ali, and some said the first among men was Abu Bakr while Ali accepted Islam as a young boy [tirmidhi:3734]. A qualified scholar can explain how these reports are reconciled.

Question: What are the 10 major signs before qiyamah?

The Prophet ﷺ said the Hour will not come until there are ten signs, and this narration names the Dajjal, the smoke, and the rising of the sun from the west [ibnmajah:4041]. I'm not sure about the remaining seven signs, because the text of this narration in the sources here mentions only these three.

Question: Who will the Prophet intercede for, and can I ask a pious dead person to intercede for me?

He ﷺ said he will be the first intercessor and the first whose intercession is accepted [abudawud:4673]. I'm not sure about asking a dead pious person to intercede; these sources don't address that, so please ask a qualified scholar.

(ar) أَخْبَرَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ حَبِيبِ بْنِ عَرَبِيٍّ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، وَالْحَارِثُ بْنُ مِسْكِينٍ، قِرَاءَةً عَلَيْهِ وَأَنَا أَسْمَعُ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْقَاسِمِ، حَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، ح وَأَخْبَرَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ مَنْصُورٍ، قَالَ أَنْبَأَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ الْمُبَارَكِ، - وَاللَّفْظُ لَهُ - عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ بْنِ وَقَّاصٍ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ، - رضى الله عنه - قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّةِ وَإِنَّمَا لاِمْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى فَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَإِلَى رَسُولِهِ فَهِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَإِلَى رَسُولِهِ وَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى دُنْيَا يُصِيبُهَا أَوِ امْرَأَةٍ يَنْكِحُهَا فَهِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى مَا هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏

[tirmidhi:2655] Jami at-Tirmidhi 2655
Grading: Daif (Ahmad Muhammad Shakir); Daif (Al-Albani); Daif (Zubair Ali Zai)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ نَصْرِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ، حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبَّادٍ الْهُنَائِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْمُبَارَكِ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ السِّخْتِيَانِيِّ، عَنْ خَالِدِ بْنِ دُرَيْكٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ عِلْمًا لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ أَوْ أَرَادَ بِهِ غَيْرَ اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَفِي الْبَابِ عَنْ جَابِرٍ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو عِيسَى هَذَا حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ غَرِيبٌ لاَ نَعْرِفُهُ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَيُّوبَ إِلاَّ مِنْ هَذَا الْوَجْهِ ‏.‏

[ibnmajah:4227] Sunan Ibn Majah 4227
Grading: Sahih (Al-Albani); Sahih (Muhammad Fouad Abd al-Baqi); Sahih (Shuaib Al Arnaut)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا يَزِيدُ بْنُ هَارُونَ، ح وَحَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ رُمْحٍ، أَنْبَأَنَا اللَّيْثُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، قَالاَ أَنْبَأَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، أَنَّ مُحَمَّدَ بْنَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ التَّيْمِيَّ، أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّهُ، سَمِعَ عَلْقَمَةَ بْنَ وَقَّاصٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، وَهُوَ يَخْطُبُ النَّاسَ فَقَالَ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ يَقُولُ ‏:‏ ‏ "‏ إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ وَلِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى فَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَإِلَى رَسُولِهِ فَهِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَإِلَى رَسُولِهِ وَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ لِدُنْيَا يُصِيبُهَا أَوِ امْرَأَةٍ يَتَزَوَّجُهَا، فَهِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى مَا هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏

[muslim:337] Sahih Muslim 337 (Abd al-Baqi no. 130)
(ar) وَحَدَّثَنَا أَبُو كُرَيْبٍ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو خَالِدٍ الأَحْمَرُ، عَنْ هِشَامٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ مَنْ هَمَّ بِحَسَنَةٍ فَلَمْ يَعْمَلْهَا كُتِبَتْ لَهُ حَسَنَةً وَمَنْ هَمَّ بِحَسَنَةٍ فَعَمِلَهَا كُتِبَتْ لَهُ عَشْرًا إِلَى سَبْعِمِائَةِ ضِعْفٍ وَمَنْ هَمَّ بِسَيِّئَةٍ فَلَمْ يَعْمَلْهَا لَمْ تُكْتَبْ وَإِنْ عَمِلَهَا كُتِبَتْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏

Question: If I do a good deed but partly to impress people, does my intention really matter that much?

Yes, intention is central. The Prophet ﷺ said that actions are only by intentions and every person will have only what he intended [nasai:75]. He gave the example of emigration: whoever emigrated for Allah and His Messenger, his emigration is for Allah and His Messenger, and whoever emigrated for some worldly gain or to marry a woman, his emigration is for what he emigrated for [nasai:75]. Umar narrated the same hadith from the pulpit, as recorded in Ibn Majah [ibnmajah:4227]. So the reward of a deed follows the intention behind it [ibnmajah:4227].

Daif (Al-Albani); Daif (Zubair Ali Zai) (ar) حَدَّثَنَا سُوَيْدُ بْنُ نَصْرٍ، أَخْبَرَنَا ابْنُ الْمُبَارَكِ، عَنِ الْمُثَنَّى بْنِ الصَّبَّاحِ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ، عَنْ جَدِّهِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ خَصْلَتَانِ مَنْ كَانَتَا فِيهِ كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ شَاكِرًا صَابِرًا وَمَنْ لَمْ تَكُونَا فِيهِ لَمْ يَكْتُبْهُ اللَّهُ شَاكِرًا وَلاَ صَابِرًا مَنْ نَظَرَ فِي دِينِهِ إِلَى مَنْ هُوَ فَوْقَهُ فَاقْتَدَى بِهِ وَنَظَرَ فِي دُنْيَاهُ إِلَى مَنْ هُوَ دُونَهُ فَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ عَلَى مَا فَضَّلَهُ بِهِ عَلَيْهِ كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ شَاكِرًا صَابِرًا وَمَنْ نَظَرَ فِي دِينِهِ إِلَى مَنْ هُوَ دُونَهُ وَنَظَرَ فِي دُنْيَاهُ إِلَى مَنْ هُوَ فَوْقَهُ فَأَسِفَ عَلَى مَا فَاتَهُ مِنْهُ لَمْ يَكْتُبْهُ اللَّهُ شَاكِرًا وَلاَ صَابِرًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ أَخْبَرَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ حِزَامٍ الرَّجُلُ الصَّالِحُ، حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ، أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ الْمُبَارَكِ، أَخْبَرَنَا الْمُثَنَّى بْنُ الصَّبَّاحِ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ جَدِّهِ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَحْوَهُ ‏.‏ قَالَ هَذَا حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ غَرِيبٌ وَلَمْ يَذْكُرْ سُوَيْدُ بْنُ نَصْرٍ فِي حَدِيثِهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ ‏.‏ Question: do I get reward for a good deed I planned but couldn't actually do?

Yes. The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever intends a good deed but does not do it has one good deed recorded for him, and whoever intends it and does it has ten up to seven hundred recorded [muslim:337]. In the narration he related from his Lord, Allah writes the intended but unperformed good deed as a complete good deed with Himself [nawawi:37]. As for an evil deed that is intended but not done, nothing is recorded against the person according to Muslim's narration, and if he does it, it is recorded as one [muslim:337].

Question: virtues of seeking Islamic knowledge?

The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever takes a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise [tirmidhi:2646]. In the narration of Abu ad-Darda, he added that the angels lower their wings out of pleasure with the seeker of knowledge, and that those in the heavens and the earth ask forgiveness for the scholar [tirmidhi:2682]. Abu Dawud's version ends with the reminder that the one whose deeds slow him down will not be sped up by his lineage [abudawud:3643].

Question: What dua does the Quran teach for increasing knowledge?

In Surat Ta-Ha Allah teaches this supplication: "My Lord! Increase me in knowledge" [quran:20:114]. Jalalayn explains that the increase meant here is in knowledge of the revelation, so that every time a part of it was sent down, his knowledge grew [jalalayn:20:114]. The same verse also instructs him not to hasten with the recitation before the revelation to him is completed [quran:20:114].

Question: How will knowledge be taken away near the end of time?

The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah does not take knowledge away by snatching it out of people's hearts, but by taking away the scholars [muslim:6796]. When no scholar remains, people take ignorant leaders who are asked and give rulings without knowledge, so they go astray and lead others astray [muslim:6796]. Bukhari records the same warning, that knowledge is removed through the death of the learned [bukhari:100].

Question: I'm studying computer science for a career, is that counted as seeking knowledge for other than Allah and will I be punished?

There is a narration in Tirmidhi that whoever learns knowledge for other than Allah, or intends by it other than Allah, should take his seat in the Fire, but it is graded weak (Da'if) [tirmidhi:2655]. A sahih narration says that whoever takes a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes a path to Paradise easy for him [tirmidhi:2646]. I'm not sure whether worldly subjects like computer science fall under these narrations; the sources don't say, so a qualified scholar is the right person to ask.

Question: What kind of knowledge did the Prophet seek refuge from?

The Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge in Allah from four things: knowledge that does not benefit, a heart that is not humble, a supplication that is not heard, and a soul that is never satisfied [nasai:5442]. He also told people to ask Allah for beneficial knowledge and seek refuge from knowledge that does not benefit [ibnmajah:3843].

Question: how happy is Allah when someone repents? heard about a lost camel example

The Prophet ﷺ said Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than one of you would be on finding a camel he had lost [muslim:6953]. Nu'man ibn Bashir's narration describes it in detail: a man travelling with his food and drink on his camel stops in a waterless desert, falls asleep under a tree, and wakes to find the camel gone [muslim:6958]. Allah's pleasure at a believer's repentance is greater than that man's joy when he finds it again [muslim:6958]. Anas narrated the same comparison in Bukhari [bukhari:6309].

Question: I've done really bad sins for years. Can Allah actually forgive all of that?

Yes. In a hadith qudsi Allah says: O son of Adam, as long as you call on Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you whatever you have done and I do not mind [qudsi:34]. Even if your sins reached the clouds of the sky and you then asked forgiveness, He would forgive you, and if you came with sins nearly filling the earth but met Him without associating anything with Him, He would bring forgiveness nearly as great [qudsi:34]. The Quran adds that for whoever repents, believes and does righteous work, "Allah will change their evil deeds to good deeds" [quran:25:70]. Jalalayn says this exchange takes place in the Hereafter [jalalayn:25:70].

Question: when is it too late to repent?

Allah says repentance is not for those who keep doing evil until death comes and then say "Lo! I repent now", nor for those who die as disbelievers [quran:4:18]. Jalalayn explains that the accepted repentance is the one made soon, before the death rattle reaches the throat [jalalayn:4:17]. For the world as a whole, the Prophet ﷺ said that whoever repents before the sun rises from the west, Allah accepts his repentance [muslim:6861]. Until then, as he ﷺ said, Allah stretches out His hand at night so that whoever sinned in the day may repent, and in the day for whoever sinned at night [muslim:6989].

Question: Did the Prophet really ask forgiveness 100 times a day even though he was sinless?

Yes. The Prophet ﷺ said that a covering sometimes comes over his heart and he seeks Allah's forgiveness a hundred times a day [muslim:6858]. He also said he seeks Allah's forgiveness and repents to Him one hundred times each day [ibnmajah:3815].

Question: What does tawbah nasuha mean, and do I need to confess my sins to someone?

Allah says: "O ye who believe! Turn unto Allah in sincere repentance!" [quran:66:8]. Jalalayn explains that a sincere (nasuh) repentance is a true one, where the person does not go back to the sin and does not intend to return to it [jalalayn:66:8]. The Prophet ﷺ said every son of Adam sins and the best of sinners are those who repent; this hadith is graded Hasan [tirmidhi:2499]. I'm not sure about confessing your sins to another person; none of these sources mentions it.

Question: I keep falling into the same sin after I repent. Is my tawbah even valid?

Allah praises those who, after doing wrong, remember Him, ask forgiveness, "and will not knowingly repeat (the wrong) they did" [quran:3:135]. Jalalayn explains that not persisting means they stop the sin rather than continuing in it [jalalayn:3:135]. The Prophet ﷺ said every son of Adam sins and the best of sinners are those who repent, a hadith graded Hasan [tirmidhi:2499]. There is also a narration that whoever seeks forgiveness is not counted as persisting even if he returns seventy times a day, but it is graded weak (Da'if) [tirmidhi:3559]. So keep repenting each time and keep striving to stop [tirmidhi:2499].

[quran:66:8] Quran 66:8 (At-Tahrim)
(ar) يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا تُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَوْبَةً نَصُوحًا عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يُكَفِّرَ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ يَوْمَ لَا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ ۖ نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَىٰ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَانِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

[ibnkathir:31:12] Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Arabic) on 31:12 (Luqman)
(ar) اخْتَلَفَ السَّلَفُ فِي لُقْمَانَ، عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: هَلْ كَانَ نَبِيًّا، أَوْ عَبْدًا صَالِحًا مِنْ غَيْرِ نُبُوَّةٍ؟ عَلَى قَوْلَيْنِ، الْأَكْثَرُونَ عَلَى الثَّانِي.
وَقَالَ سُفْيَانُ الثَّوْرِيُّ، عَنِ الْأَشْعَثِ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَة، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ: كَانَ لُقْمَانُ عَبْدًا حَبَشِيًّا نَجَّارًا.
وَقَالَ قَتَادَةُ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ، قُلْتُ لِجَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: مَا انْتَهَى إِلَيْكُمْ مِنْ شَأْنِ لُقْمَانَ؟ قَالَ: كَانَ قَصِيرًا أَفْطَسَ مِنَ النُّوبَةِ.
وَقَالَ يَحْيَى بْنُ سَعِيدٍ الْأَنْصَارِيُّ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ قَالَ: كَانَ لُقْمَانُ مِنْ سُودَانِ مِصْرَ، ذَا مَشَافِرَ، أَعْطَاهُ اللَّهُ الْحِكْمَةَ وَمَنَعَهُ النُّبُوَّةَ.
وَقَالَ الْأَوْزَاعِيُّ: رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ، حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ حَرْمَلة قَالَ: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ أَسْوَدُ إِلَى سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ يَسْأَلُهُ، فَقَالَ لَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ الْمُسَيَّبِ: لَا تَحْزَنْ مِنْ أَجْلِ أَنَّكَ أَسْوَدَ، فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ مِنْ أَخْيَرِ النَّاسِ ثَلَاثَةٌ مِنَ السُّودَانِ: بِلَالٌ، ومهْجَع مَوْلَى عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ، وَلُقْمَانُ الْحَكِيمُ، كَانَ أَسْوَدَ نُوبِيًّا ذَا مَشَافِرَ  .

[ibnkathir:31:12.2] Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Arabic) on 31:12 (part 2) (Luqman)
(ar) وَقَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ وَكِيع، حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، عَنْ أَبِي الْأَشْهَبِ  ، عَنْ خَالِدٍ الرَّبَعِيّ قَالَ: كَانَ لُقْمَانُ عَبْدًا حَبَشِيًّا نَجَّارًا، فَقَالَ لَهُ مَوْلَاهُ: اذْبَحْ لَنَا هَذِهِ الشَّاةِ. فَذَبَحَهَا، فَقَالَ: أخْرجْ أَطْيَبَ مُضغتين فِيهَا. فَأَخْرَجَ اللِّسَانَ وَالْقَلْبَ، فَمَكَثَ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ: اذْبَحْ لَنَا هَذِهِ الشَّاةَ. فَذَبَحَهَا، فَقَالَ: أَخْرِجْ أَخْبَثَ مُضْغَتَيْنِ فِيهَا. فَأَخْرَجَ اللِّسَانَ وَالْقَلْبَ، فَقَالَ لَهُ مَوْلَاهُ: أَمَرْتُكَ أَنْ تخرج أطيب مُضْغَتَيْنِ فِيهَا فَأَخْرَجْتَهُمَا، وَأَمَرْتُكَ أَنْ تُخْرِجَ أَخْبَثَ مُضْغَتَيْنِ فِيهَا فَأَخْرَجْتَهُمَا. فَقَالَ لُقْمَانُ: إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ شَيْءٍ أَطْيَبَ مِنْهُمَا إِذَا طَابَا، وَلَا أَخْبَثَ مِنْهُمَا إِذَا خَبُثا  .
وَقَالَ شُعْبَةُ، عَنِ الْحَكَمِ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ: كَانَ لُقْمَانُ عَبْدًا صَالِحًا، وَلَمْ يَكُنْ نَبِيًّا.
وَقَالَ الْأَعْمَشُ: قَالَ مُجَاهِدٌ: كَانَ لُقْمَانُ عَبْدًا أَسْوَدَ عَظِيمَ الشَّفَتَيْنِ، مُشَقَّقَ الْقَدَمَيْنِ.

Question: Was Luqman a prophet or just a wise man?

Allah says: "And verily We gave Luqman wisdom" [quran:31:12]. Ibn Kathir explains that the early generations differed over whether Luqman was a prophet or a righteous servant without prophethood, and that most held the second view [ibnkathir:31:12]. Mujahid is reported saying he was a righteous servant and not a prophet [ibnkathir:31:12.2]. The view that he was a prophet is transmitted from Ikrimah, but Ibn Kathir notes that its chain includes a weak narrator [ibnkathir:31:12.4]. Since the early scholars held both views, please ask a qualified scholar if you need more detail.

Question: what are the 'seven oft-repeated' (sab al mathani) in surah al-hijr?

Allah says: "We have given thee seven of the oft-repeated (verses) and the great Qur'an" [quran:15:87]. Ibn Kathir notes a difference of opinion: Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said they are the seven long surahs, al-Baqarah, Al Imran, an-Nisa, al-Ma'idah, al-An'am, al-A'raf and Yunus [ibnkathir:15:87]. The second view, reported from Umar, Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas, is that they are al-Fatihah, which is seven verses [ibnkathir:15:87.2]. Ibn Kathir then explains that calling al-Fatihah the seven mathani does not prevent the long surahs from also being described that way [ibnkathir:15:87.4]. Question: Was the verse about the Ruh (17:85) revealed in Makkah or Madinah?

The reports differ. Ibn Mas'ud narrated that he was walking with the Prophet ﷺ in a field in Madinah when some Jews asked him about the spirit, and after a pause the verse "ويسألونك عن الروح" was recited in reply [ibnkathir:17:85]. Ibn Kathir notes that this suggests the verse is Madinan even though the whole surah is Makkan, and he mentions that it may have been revealed a second time in Madinah, or that he was inspired to answer with a verse already revealed [ibnkathir:17:85.2]. He also cites Ibn Abbas saying that Quraysh asked the Jews for a question to test him, were told to ask about the spirit, and the verse was revealed, which points to Makkah [ibnkathir:17:85.2]. A qualified scholar can explain how these reports fit together.

Question: how long was prophet Ayyub sick for?

The Quran mentions Ayyub crying out to his Lord that adversity had afflicted him, without giving a length of time [quran:21:83]. Jalalayn says the trial, in which he lost his wealth and children and was abandoned by all but his wife, lasted three, seven or eighteen years [jalalayn:21:83]. Ibn Kathir reports from al-Hasan and Qatadah that it was seven years and some months, and from Wahb ibn Munabbih that it was three years exactly [ibnkathir:21:83.3]. He also cites a narration attributed to the Prophet ﷺ through Anas that his trial lasted eighteen years [ibnkathir:21:83.8]. Since the reports differ, please ask a qualified scholar if you need to go further.

Question: how many days was Yunus inside the fish?

Allah says "the fish swallowed him" [quran:37:142], and then "We cast him on a desert shore while he was sick" [quran:37:145]. The verses do not state how long he stayed inside. Jalalayn records several opinions about when he was cast out onto the shore: the same day, or after three, seven, twenty or forty days [jalalayn:37:145]. Jalalayn also explains that had he not glorified Allah, the belly of the fish would have become his grave until the Day of Resurrection [jalalayn:37:144]. Since the scholars gave different durations, a qualified scholar can help if you want to research it.

Question: What did Allah give Dawud with iron, and was he also a king?

Allah says: "And We made the iron supple unto him" [quran:34:10]. Jalalayn explains that iron became like dough in his hands [jalalayn:34:10]. He was told to make long coats of mail and measure their links [quran:34:11], and Jalalayn explains this as full-length armour whose rings are made to fit one another [jalalayn:34:11]. Jalalayn also says the favour given to him included prophethood and a scripture, and that the mountains and birds glorified Allah with him [jalalayn:34:10]. I'm not sure about his kingship; these sources do not mention it.

Question: How old was the Prophet ﷺ when he passed away?

The narrations here say he was sixty-three. Ibn Abbas said revelation came to him at forty, he stayed in Makkah thirteen years and in Madinah ten, and he died at sixty-three [tirmidhi:3621]. Aishah also said he died at sixty-three [tirmidhi:3654]. There is another report from Ibn Abbas that he died at sixty-five, but it is graded Shadh, meaning it goes against the stronger narrations [tirmidhi:3651].

Question: Are there any situations where lying is actually allowed in Islam?

Yes, a narration names three. The Prophet ﷺ said lying is not lawful except in three cases: what a man says to his wife to please her, lying in war, and lying to make peace between people [tirmidhi:1939]. Outside such cases the general rule is strict: he ﷺ warned that lying leads to wickedness and wickedness to the Fire, and that a person who keeps lying is written down with Allah as a liar [tirmidhi:1971]. So these are narrow exceptions and do not make lying ordinary [tirmidhi:1939].

Question: Is there reward in being kind to animals?

Yes. The Prophet ﷺ told of a man who climbed down a well to give water in his shoe to a dog dying of thirst, and Allah thanked him and forgave him [bukhari:2466]. When the companions asked whether there is reward for serving animals, he said there is reward in serving every living creature [bukhari:2466]. In another narration a woman of bad character was forgiven for giving water to a thirsty dog [muslim:5860]. The opposite is also warned against: a woman was punished because of a cat she neither fed nor let free to find food [muslim:5855].

Question: Allah's mercy is divided into 100 parts? whats the hadith

The Prophet ﷺ said Allah has one hundred parts of mercy, and He sent down one of them among jinn, humans, animals and insects [muslim:6974]. Because of that one part, creatures love and show kindness to one another, and even a wild animal is gentle with its young [muslim:6974]. Allah kept the other ninety-nine parts with Himself for His servants on the Day of Resurrection [muslim:6973].

Question: Do angels attend our prayers and gatherings where Quran is studied?

Yes. The Prophet ﷺ said groups of angels take turns among people by night and by day and meet together at the Fajr and Asr prayers; those who stayed the night ascend, and Allah asks them how they left His servants, and they say they left them praying and found them praying [bukhari:7429]. He ﷺ also said that no people sit remembering Allah except that the angels surround them, mercy covers them, tranquility descends on them and Allah mentions them to those with Him [ibnmajah:3791]. Abu Dawud records the same blessings for people gathered in a mosque reciting and studying the Book of Allah together [abudawud:1455].

Question: What did the Prophet say to Abu Bakr in the cave during the hijrah?

Abu Bakr said that if one of the pursuers looked down at his feet he would see them, and the Prophet ﷺ replied: "يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ مَا ظَنُّكَ بِاثْنَيْنِ اللَّهُ ثَالِثُهُمَا", meaning what do you think of two whose third is Allah [tirmidhi:3096]. Muslim records the same exchange in the cave [muslim:6169].

Question: did the Prophet manage to conquer Taif when he besieged it?

No. When the Prophet ﷺ besieged Ta'if and could not take it, he said they would return, the companions disliked leaving, so he told them to fight the next day and many were wounded [bukhari:4325]. When he again said they would return the next day, they were pleased, and he smiled [bukhari:4325].

Question: How many sahaba fought at Badr?

The narrations give the number slightly differently. Al-Bara is reported in Tirmidhi saying they used to say the people of Badr were three hundred and thirteen men, the same number as the companions of Talut [tirmidhi:1598]. In Ibn Majah, al-Bara says they were three hundred and ten and some, like the companions of Talut who crossed the river with him, and none crossed with him but a believer [ibnmajah:2828]. Both narrations are from the same companion and both are graded sahih [ibnmajah:2828]. A qualified scholar can explain how the wordings are reconciled.

Question: What are angels made of, and do they eat or sleep?

The Prophet ﷺ said the angels were created from light, the jinn from smokeless fire, and Adam from what you have been told [muslim:7495]. The Quran describes angels who "resist not Allah in that which He commandeth them, but do that which they are commanded" [quran:66:6], and says Allah makes them messengers "having wings two, three and four" [quran:35:1]. I'm not sure whether angels eat or sleep, since these sources do not say.

Question: What do Munkar and Nakir ask in the grave? And what if a person never learned Arabic, will they understand?

The Prophet ﷺ said that when the dead are buried, two angels come, one called al-Munkar and the other an-Nakir, and ask what he used to say about this man [tirmidhi:1071]. The believer testifies that he is the servant and Messenger of Allah, and his grave is widened and lit; the hypocrite says he heard people say something and said the same, and he is punished until he is raised; the hadith is graded Hasan [tirmidhi:1071]. I'm not sure about the language of the questioning; this narration does not mention it.

Question: Which holy books did Allah reveal, and did Ibrahim also get a book?

Allah says He gave Isa the Gospel, "wherein is guidance and a light", confirming the Torah before it [quran:5:46]. He says "unto David We gave the Psalms" [quran:17:55]. And to the Prophet ﷺ He revealed the Scripture "confirming whatever Scripture was before it, and a watcher over it" [quran:5:48]. I'm not sure whether Ibrahim was given a book; these verses do not mention one, so please check with a qualified scholar.

Question: How many wings does Jibril have, and can he appear in human form?

Jalalayn explains that among the great signs the Prophet ﷺ saw on that night was Jibril with six hundred wings [jalalayn:53:18]. Aishah said that what the Prophet ﷺ saw was Jibril in his true form, filling the horizon [bukhari:3234]. I'm not sure about Jibril appearing in human form; these sources do not mention that.

Question: Is cutting off relatives a sin? And how often am I required to visit them?

Yes, it is serious. The Prophet ﷺ said the womb (kinship) takes its name from Ar-Rahman, so whoever keeps ties with it, Allah keeps ties with him, and whoever cuts it, Allah cuts him off [tirmidhi:1924]. I'm not sure how often visits are required; these sources do not set any frequency, so please ask a qualified scholar.

Question: A woman was forgiven for giving water to a dog. So can I keep a dog as a pet at home?

The Prophet ﷺ told of a woman who saw a dog circling a well on a hot day with its tongue out from thirst, drew water for it in her shoe, and was forgiven [muslim:5860]. Bukhari records the same story [bukhari:3467]. I'm not sure about keeping a dog as a pet; this story is about mercy to an animal and does not address keeping one, so please ask a qualified scholar.

Question: What did the Prophet say in the farewell sermon, and how many people were there?

During the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet ﷺ asked whether this was not the most sacred day, month and land, and then said that their blood and their wealth are as sacred to them as that day, in that month, in that land [ibnmajah:3931]. He asked whether he had conveyed the message and they said yes [ibnmajah:3931]. I'm not sure how many people attended; this narration does not give a number.

(ar) حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو حَفْصٍ، عَمْرُو بْنُ عَلِيٍّ حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ، عَنِ الْعَلاَءِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ آيَةُ الْمُنَافِقِ ثَلاَثٌ إِذَا حَدَّثَ كَذَبَ وَإِذَا وَعَدَ أَخْلَفَ وَإِذَا اؤْتُمِنَ خَانَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو عِيسَى هَذَا حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ غَرِيبٌ مِنْ حَدِيثِ الْعَلاَءِ وَقَدْ رُوِيَ مِنْ غَيْرِ وَجْهٍ عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏ وَفِي الْبَابِ عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ وَأَنَسٍ وَجَابِرٍ ‏.‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ حُجْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي سُهَيْلِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَحْوَهُ بِمَعْنَاهُ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو عِيسَى هَذَا حَدِيثٌ صَحِيحٌ وَأَبُو سُهَيْلٍ هُوَ عَمُّ مَالِكِ بْنِ أَنَسٍ وَاسْمُهُ نَافِعُ بْنُ مَالِكِ بْنِ أَبِي عَامِرٍ الأَصْبَحِيُّ الْخَوْلاَنِيُّ ‏.‏

Question: Is breaking a promise a major sin? What if I promised but circumstances made it impossible?

The Prophet ﷺ counted breaking promises among the signs of a hypocrite, together with lying when speaking and betraying a trust [tirmidhi:2631]. An-Nasa'i records the same three signs [nasai:5021]. I'm not sure about a promise that becomes impossible to keep because of circumstances; these sources do not discuss that case.
